questions.q: Why is execution accuracy measured on a held-out set instead of the training questions?
options: Held-out questions are easier to answer
Scoring on training questions would measure memorization rather than generalization
The training questions don't have gold SQL available
Held-out sets don't require a sandboxed database
questions.explain: A held-out set, untouched by SFT or RLHF, is needed to measure how well the model generalizes to new questions rather than how well it memorized training examples.

questions.q: What two checkpoints does this lesson's comparison evaluate?
options: Two different base models
The SFT-only checkpoint from Lesson 16 and the RLHF checkpoint from Lesson 18
Project 1's RL policy and Project 2's reward model
Two different reward functions
questions.explain: The comparison runs execution accuracy on the identical held-out set for both the SFT-only checkpoint and the RLHF checkpoint.

questions.q: What is the schema-hallucination regression this lesson checks for?
options: The model refusing to answer any question
RLHF pushing the model toward referencing a table or column name that doesn't actually exist in the schema
The model always returning an empty result set
The model switching from AdventureWorks2012 to Northwind at random
questions.explain: Because the execution reward only checks result sets, RLHF can inadvertently push the model toward hallucinating plausible but nonexistent table or column names.

questions.q: How is the schema-hallucination regression caught?
options: By asking a human to read every output
By validating a generated query's table and column references against the actual schema metadata
By increasing the learning rate during RLHF
It cannot be detected automatically
questions.explain: Validating referenced names against schema metadata, separately from execution, directly measures a hallucination rate for each checkpoint.

questions.q: If RLHF improves held-out accuracy but also increases the hallucination rate on failing queries, how should this be reported?
options: As a failed project that should not be reported
Only the accuracy number should be reported, since it is the more flattering one
As a complete and honest finding — both the accuracy improvement and the hallucination regression are real results worth reporting side by side
The hallucination finding should be hidden from the write-up
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames a mixed result — accuracy gain plus a hallucination regression — as a complete, honest finding, not something to hide or treat as failure.
